Nanum CSV Viewer — Quick Guide
[Open] • File ▸ Open… (Ctrl+O) opens .csv / .txt as well as Excel (.xlsx/.xls), SAS (.sas7bdat), and SPSS (.sav). • The first page appears instantly; the rest is indexed in the background (progress bar at the bottom). You can scroll while indexing. • Multi-sheet Excel workbooks switch via the sheet tabs directly under the grid (they no longer stretch under the Workspace Explorer or the AI panel). • For SPSS/SAS, View ▸ Field Labels swaps codes and names for value labels and variable labels. • SPSS/SAS declared types (currency, percent, date, categorical, ordinal…) are matched automatically; currency and percent columns show their symbols.
[Encoding] • Auto-detected (UTF-8 / UTF-8 BOM / CP949·EUC-KR). If wrong, click the encoding widget at the right of the status bar, or use Data ▸ Encoding. No re-indexing needed.
[Find] • Type in the Find box and press Enter, or F3, to jump to the next match (case-insensitive, wraps around).
[Filter] • Use the funnel icon on a header for type-aware filters: range for numbers/time, checkboxes for categories/booleans, text predicates (contains/regex/list/blank) for strings/identifiers. • Active conditions appear as chips above the grid — remove with ✕, click to edit, toggle ALL (AND) / ANY (OR). • Filter by This Cell Value (Ctrl+B), Exclude This Value, ≥ / ≤ This Value (right-click a cell; ≥/≤ follow the column type — numbers, dates, text) and the Advanced expression filter (Ctrl+Shift+F; NOT/AND/OR/parentheses; regex via matches / matches_cs / !matches; * = any column, e.g. * matches "x"). A regex that times out on a cell counts that cell as non-matching and is reported with ⚠. Clear Filter removes all.
[Sort] • Click a column header to sort (click again to toggle direction). • Shift+Click headers to sort by multiple columns (priority shown on each header). • Equal values keep their original order (stable sort). Clear Sort restores file order.
[Analysis] • Facets panel (toolbar button, View ▸ Facets Panel, or F6): see per-column distributions (histogram / top values) and click a bar to filter instantly (cross-filtering). • Data / Statistics / Visualization menus: distributions, correlation, tests, models, group aggregation, pivot table (Data) and pivot chart (Visualization). Export: File ▸ Export View ▸ CSV/Markdown/JSON/HTML. • Settings ▸ Files & Data ▸ Analysis memory cap: the memory budget for analyses computed in memory (basic statistics, charts, group-by, duplicates, chi-square, pivot, data-quality reference sets, advanced statistics). Auto (default) is 50% of this PC's physical memory, at least 512 MB, with no upper limit; Manual sets a value in GB (up to the physical memory). A value above the currently available memory shows a warning. When an analysis exceeds the budget, choose Yes in the message to open Settings.
[Detail Panel] • Toggle with the toolbar button, View ▸ Row Detail Panel, or F4 (off at startup unless you turn it on in Settings ▸ Panels & Layout). Shows every column of the selected row as name + value — handy for cells with line breaks.
[Status Light] • The colored dot at the right end of the status bar: ⚪ Idle · 🟡 Loading · 🟠 Busy · 🟢 Ready.
[Settings] • Tools ▸ Settings… (Ctrl+,) — General (theme system / light / dark, language auto / English / Korean; View ▸ Theme and Language also work), Panels & Layout, Grid, Files, AI Agent, Shortcuts. • At startup the Workspace Explorer and the AI panel are on; the row detail panel, facets and findings are off. Change this in Panels & Layout, or turn on "remember last state". (An existing setup that still had the old default — only the AI panel — gets the explorer once after updating; a layout you chose yourself is left as is.) While the AI panel is visible, the AI agent (omp) starts in the background a moment after the app is idle (the model, thinking and approval pickers are ready before you type); while the panel is hidden it starts only when you open the panel or send the first message. • The model button under the AI chat box lists "Recently used" models first (the last 8 you picked, newest first; omp's own usage record is read, read-only), then every model by provider. The recent ones also stay in their provider group. If omp's record cannot be read (for example after an omp update changes its format), the chat shows a one-time notice per omp version and only the full list is shown; Settings ▸ AI Agent shows the status. • The "+" at the bottom-left of the AI chat box adds files or a folder to the workspace (Add files… / Add folder…), and you can also drop files or a folder onto the chat. Only data files are added (CSV/TSV/TXT, Excel, SAS, SPSS, SQLite; a folder contributes the data files directly in it, and more than 10 asks first); other files are listed in a notice and skipped. No tabs open. The files appear as chips above the box; your next message tells the agent their table names (never their contents), and the chips clear after sending. Removing a chip only drops it from that message.
[Workspace (several files)] • Each open file is a tab: Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab switch, Ctrl+W or middle-click closes. A workbook (Excel/SAS/SPSS/SQLite) is one tab with sheet buttons at the bottom. • View ▸ Workspace Explorer (Ctrl+Shift+W) lists sources, tables and views. Add a data file as a source, then join, append, compare or group with the wizards (join diagnostics show unmatched/duplicate keys first). • In the Workspace Explorer a single click selects a tab like the tab strip: an open file, view or result switches to its tab, a table that is not open yet is opened (a workbook sheet switches the workbook tab to that sheet), and a column selects that column in the grid (a hidden column is only reported). Arrow keys only move the selection, Enter opens, and switching tabs or sheets selects the matching node. • Workspace ▸ New Query (Ctrl+Alt+Q) opens the SQL editor (DuckDB; a single SELECT only). CSV columns are typed in table "T"; "T__raw" keeps every column as original text. ID-like columns are text — use CAST("id" AS BIGINT) to compare numerically. • Views are read-only tabs (save as a file, then open it, to edit). ⚠ marks a stale view; refresh recomputes it and resets that tab's filters/sort. A source used by a view cannot be renamed or removed. • File ▸ Open Workspace… (Ctrl+Shift+O) / Save Workspace (Ctrl+S; asks for a name the first time) store sources and view definitions — and the panel layout — in a .ncvws file (data is not stored; Locate/Skip for missing files). Opening a workspace restores its own layout instead of the app defaults. File ▸ Close Workspace (after the save prompt) closes all tabs, sources and views and returns to the app's startup panel layout. • File ▸ New Workspace… (Ctrl+Shift+N) asks to save pending changes, then a dialog takes the location, the name, and previews the .ncvws path and the analysis folder (<name>_분석결과). "Include currently open files" (off by default) keeps the open file tabs and registers them as sources; otherwise every tab and the current workspace are closed. The new .ncvws is written immediately, the AI agent starts a new conversation with the new analysis folder, and the panels return to the app's startup layout. • Workspace ▸ Workspace Notes… stores free text (data description, key relations, analysis goals; up to 20,000 characters) in the .ncvws file. The AI agent reads it (ws.notes) as user-written data — it never overrides the data policy, approval mode or your requests. • A saved .ncvws (format v2) also remembers the AI agent's conversation (session link), the workspace's approval mode / data sharing / local Python settings, and who created each view. Opening the workspace resumes that conversation; if it no longer exists (e.g. the file came from another PC) a new one starts and the chat shows a notice. Workspace ▸ Start New Conversation for This Workspace replaces the link. • Workspace agent settings can only tighten: the effective value is the stricter of the app setting and the workspace value (approval: always ask > edits auto > allow all; data: summary only > rows with approval > rows allowed; local Python: off > on). To loosen, change the app default (Tools ▸ Settings… ▸ AI Agent, choose "App default"). The chat shows a "🔒 Workspace" chip when the workspace limits something. • In the Workspace Explorer, views made by the AI agent show ✦ instead of ◈; the tooltip tells who created the view, when, and the request that led to it. Views from older (v1) files have no such info.
[Analysis skills & Python environment] • With local Python on (Settings ▸ AI Agent), the agent can use 20 bundled analysis skills (clinical 7, statistics 9, machine learning 3, app 1; about 550 tokens; nothing is loaded while Python is off). Turn all, a category, or single skills off under "Analysis skills"; changing it restarts the agent on the same conversation. The skills are third-party (K-Dense, MIT) instructions. • The app's validated tools and menu analyses come first; Python is for analyses the app lacks or when you ask for it. Python results carry the "Python analysis (outside the app's validated tools)" label and a reproducibility header. Even with Summary only, Python output can reach the model — this is guidance, not a hard guarantee. • Settings ▸ AI ▸ Python environment installs an app-managed venv (pinned versions, prebuilt wheels only; 64-bit Intel/AMD Python 3.10–3.13) by group. The agent asks for packages with py.ensure_packages and you approve. • Tools ▸ Export Python Analysis Bundle…: exports scripts, report, figures and requirements.lock to a folder/zip (data excluded by default).
[AI setup & troubleshooting] • Tools ▸ AI Setup Assistant… (also the button of the same name in Settings ▸ AI Agent) checks, in order, ① WebView2 ② omp ③ sign-in ④ connection test, and fixes the failing step on the spot. When the AI panel cannot start it opens by itself once per app version (turn that off with "Don't show this automatically again"). The connection test sends no message to any model. • If omp is not found: use Browse… to pick omp.exe, Install this copy to copy an omp-windows-x64.exe found in Downloads or on PATH, or Download omp to fetch GitHub's latest release (SHA-256 verified, installed to %LOCALAPPDATA%\omp\omp.exe; minimum 18.4.4). Tick "Also add it to my user PATH" to run omp in a terminal too. omp is not code-signed, so Windows may warn. A PC with only the omp.ps1 wrapper needs omp.exe. • In the sign-in step press Sign in next to a provider; the authorization page opens in your browser. Providers that need an API key: set the provider's environment variable (for example ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) and restart the app, or run omp login in a terminal. The Sign in… button of the chat's "No AI model is available" notice opens this step too. • If the chat screen does not start (WebView2): when it says the runtime is missing, install it from the download page and press Retry. For error 0x8007139F a compatibility setting may be the cause: press Remove setting (current-user entries only; a backup .reg is saved first), then Retry. Access denied means checking the permissions of the WebView2 data folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\NanumCsvViewer\WebView2). Failures are logged to %LOCALAPPDATA%\NanumCsvViewer\agent\webview2-init.log (for support: the environment variable NANUMCSV_WEBVIEW2_LOG=1 also writes the browser log). • Help ▸ Copy AI Diagnostics copies the app, OS, WebView2, omp, settings and recent logs to the clipboard (user name, keys and tokens are masked, but masking is pattern-based, so check before pasting; no cell values or other data contents are included).
[Context menus] • Right-click a cell: Copy, Filter ▸ (this value / exclude / ≥ / ≤), sort this column, hide column, conditional formatting, Ask AI ▸ (summarize the column / analyze rows with this value — opens the AI panel and sends the question), plus the edit commands (disabled until Sheet Edit is on; "Turn On Sheet Edit" is at the top). • Right-click a column header: sort, filter, hide, freeze columns up to here, auto-fit width, change type, Quick Analysis ▸ (descriptive / frequency / distribution for that column), and rename/insert/delete column in Sheet Edit mode. • Right-click a row number: copy the row, show the row detail, insert/delete row (Sheet Edit mode). • Right-click a tab: close, close others, close all, copy path, open folder, and workspace commands.
